## SVR Hyperparameter Search Grid (3.2)

Both SVR notebooks share the identical two-stage search defined in
`3.2 PredictionCommonGround.ipynb`, so the direct and residual results stay
directly comparable. The grid search runs only for the kernel that wins the
scan, not for all three.

| Stage | Setting | Values searched |
|-------|---------|-----------------|
| Kernel scan | Kernels | `linear`, `poly`, `rbf` |
| | Held fixed during the scan | `C = 1`, `gamma = "scale"` |
| | Selection criterion | Validation R² in count space |
| | Training sample | 4,000 rows per class (8,000 total) |
| Grid search | `C` | 1, 10, 50 |
| | `gamma` | `"scale"`, 0.05, 0.2 |
| | `degree` (polynomial kernel only) | 2, 3 |
| | Cross-validation | 3-fold |
| | Selection criterion | Count-space MAE |
| | Training sample | 8,000 rows per class (16,000 total) |
| Feature sets | Candidates | `basic`, `basic+poi`, `basic+weather`, `basic+poi+weather` |
| | Selection criterion | Validation R² in count space |
| Scoring | Validation subsample | 50,000 rows; the level's winner is re-scored on the full validation split |

: Two-stage SVR hyperparameter search grid, shared by the direct (`3.2a`) and residual (`3.2b`) models. {#tbl-svr-search-grid}

The four candidate feature sets are built from the same blocks at every level.
`basic` is hour (hourly grids only) plus calendar, location and history;
the other three add the POI and weather blocks to it.

| Block | Features | Count |
|-------|----------|------:|
| Hour (hourly grids only) | `hour_sin`, `hour_cos` | 2 |
| Calendar | `month_sin`, `month_cos`, `is_weekend`, `is_holiday`, `is_near_holiday`, `day_of_week` | 6 |
| Location | `lat`, `lon`, `distance_to_loop` | 3 |
| History | `base_demand` | 1 |
| POI | 14 `poi_cat_*` category counts | 14 |
| Weather | `2m_temp_c`, `total_precip_mm`, `snow_cov`, `snow_depth`, `wind_speed` | 5 |

: Feature blocks composing the four candidate sets. Resulting widths are 10 / 24 / 15 / 29 features on daily grids and 12 / 26 / 17 / 31 on hourly grids, for `basic` / `basic+poi` / `basic+weather` / `basic+poi+weather` respectively. {#tbl-svr-feature-blocks}

## Deep Learning Prediction (3.3)

The grid search was run independently for each of the six spatial and temporal
combinations, with the winning configuration selected by validation MAE in
count space.

| Stage | Setting | Values | Rationale |
|-------|---------|--------|-----------|
| Architecture search | Hidden Layer configurations | [64,32,16], [128,64,32], [128,64,32,16], [256,128,64,32] | Pyramid configurations outperformed equal-width configurations in initial experiments. |
| | Learning rates | 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001 | Covers three orders of magnitude to account for level-specific convergence behaviour |
| | Dropout rates | 0.0, 0.2 | Higher rates consistently hurt performance in initial tests |
| | Configurations per level | 24 (full grid) | |
| | Selection criterion | Validation MAE in count space | |
| Training | Optimizer | AdamW (weight decay 1e-4) | Decouples weight decay from the gradient update, avoiding L2 scaling issues with adaptive optimizers [@loshchilov2019decoupled]. |
| | Loss function | MSE | |
| | Batch size | 250 | |
| | Maximum epochs | 15 | |
| | Early stopping patience | 3 epochs | Stops training after three consecutive epochs without validation improvement |
| Feature set | Candidates | `basic+poi+weather` (fixed) | |
| | Hourly features | 31 total | |
| | Daily features | 29 total | |

: FNN hyperparameter search grid. {#tbl-fnn-search-grid}

| Level | Layers | Learning rate | Dropout |
|-------|--------|---------------:|--------:|
| community / hourly | 256, 128, 64, 32 | 0.001 | 0.0 |
| community / daily | 128, 64, 32, 16 | 0.01 | 0.0 |
| h3_7 / hourly | 128, 64, 32, 16 | 0.0001 | 0.0 |
| h3_7 / daily | 128, 64, 32, 16 | 0.01 | 0.2 |
| census / hourly | 64, 32, 16 | 0.001 | 0.0 |
| census / daily | 64, 32, 16 | 0.001 | 0.2 |

: Winning FNN architecture per level, selected by validation MAE in count space over a grid of four layer configurations, three learning rates, and two dropout rates (24 configurations per level). {#tbl-fnn-architecture-by-level}

| Level | MAE | RMSE | R² | Skill (MAE) | Skill (RMSE) |
|-------|----:|-----:|---:|-------------:|--------------:|
| community / hourly | 2.620 | 9.678 | 0.925 | +9.7% | +12.7% |
| h3_7 / hourly | 1.041 | 7.358 | 0.883 | +2.5% | +1.0% |
| census / hourly | 0.276 | 2.218 | 0.844 | −1.0% | −6.1% |
| community / daily | 54.518 | 190.617 | 0.921 | −10.0% | −4.8% |
| census / daily | 6.355 | 42.094 | 0.819 | −29.2% | −42.7% |
| h3_7 / daily | 28.209 | 155.722 | 0.844 | −31.9% | −28.7% |

: FNN test performance per level against the historical-mean baseline (skill = 1 − MAE_model / MAE_baseline), sorted by skill (MAE). {#tbl-fnn-level-comparison}

![Figure 4. Best DQN policy found across the five training runs. The Q-table stores entries only for states that were actually visited during training (visit_counts > 0) and thus, combinations of time step and battery level that were never reached remain empty. The DQN network, by contrast, is a continuous function that produces an output for any given input. This includes states that never occurred during training (e.g. battery=60 at t=0). Thereby, both plots differ in terms of their appearance.](plots/dqn_policy_heatmap.png){#fig-dqn_policy_heatmap}
